title: I'm building a text-to-motion tool that works on any character.
author: ppierzc
selftext:
Hey everyone,  
I’m the developer of Animatica. One of the biggest frustrations I’ve had with AI animation tools is that they are often locked to a specific skeleton or require a nightmare of a setup to retarget to the final character. I'm building this so that we can finally use text-to-motion directly on the characters in our scenes.

I’m trying to build something that actually fits into a production pipeline rather than just being a tech demo, so I thought I would share my progress on here to get some feedback :)

comments.author: sloth2121
comments.body:
I will say yes, yes… i vibe code. 
But my very first idea has turned into this elaborate scheme i may be able to get away with or I might not. 

That being said, I’ve noticed a lot of the content creations are repeats but with slight variations or methods of going about it. 

So double edged sword. 

Your post was a nice breath of fresh air, how do you plan on evolving it?

replies.author: ppierzc
replies.body: Thanks, appreciate it. I am planning to 1) improve on the quality, there are quite a few artifacts 2) expand this beyond just humans/humanoids, 3) let you bring your own style of motion, as the current version still has quite a generic motion style.

replies.author: sloth2121
replies.body: DM’d you.

comments.author: JoanofArc0531
comments.body: Does it do only humanoids only?

replies.author: ppierzc
replies.body: Currently yes, though I am planning to make it work on non humanoids as well

replies.author: Gronanor
replies.body: How do you plan to do that ? I thought most model were designed for humanoids skeleton ? Do you train your own model?

replies.author: ppierzc
replies.body: Yep, there is simply much more humanoid data out there. Though I’ve got my hands on some quadruped data, which I now have an initial model trained on using, just not yet ready to share :). It’s mostly about figuring out a more data efficient training paradigm.

replies.author: Gronanor
replies.body: As a data scientist (I'm just a game dev enthusiast), I recommend to not get your expectations too high. This is a common case of imbalanced dataset. Quite hard to solve non the less, and definitely would not recommend a unifyed model. I look forward to see what's yours results would be!

replies.author: ppierzc
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback, I’m a ML researcher myself (similarly just game dev enthusiast), working on motion research for quite a while now :) it is a difficult problem to solve, and definitely no a unified model would be a terrible idea, the distribution shift between human motion and non-humanoid calls for smaller specialized models 🙌

replies.author: ppierzc
replies.body: we're making progress, but I don't have an ETA yet :)

replies.author: ppierzc
replies.body:
Kimodo is one piece. I built four other ML models on top of it (incl. retargeting, text-to-pose) to make it actually work on any humanoid character, not just the one Kimodo was trained on.

It’s free during early access, I’m covering the GPU cost to make it easier to test. If it doesn’t bring you value, no need to pay 😉

Curious have you tried Kimodo yourself?
